source.title: Scaling Properties of Speech Language Models

record.file_problem: The full paper text is present and readable.
record.tranche_reason: The paper measures scaling laws in speech language models, an additional modality, and also compares raw speech tokens with unigram-compressed tokens.
record.gate_note: The paper reports a power-law envelope for speech-model test loss, fitted loss-law parameters, compute-optimal allocations, and downstream scaling and loss correlations. It also reports that synthetic Tiny Stories training improves semantic scores, but that result does not test scaling or predictability and is not recorded as a row. The benchmark comparisons in Table 3 include results from other works and are not recorded as this study's results.
record.test_reason: The authors train over 50 speech LMs on HuBERT tokens and fit Hoffmann/Muennighoff loss laws. They derive compute-optimal exponents and fit downstream power laws against compute and loss. This is a new modality with its own results on V1, V3, V5, V6 and V7.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors find that speech-LM loss and downstream linguistic metrics are highly correlated and scale predictably by power laws. Optimal allocation scales parameters and data equally. Speech linguistic abilities scale up to three orders of magnitude more slowly than text. sTinyStories helps semantics, while coarser unigram tokenization hurts downstream performance.
record.recipe_differences: Adapts the Hoffmann et al. and Muennighoff et al. fitted scaling-law methods to speech-token language models, with speech-specific data and tokenizer setups; it is not a reproduction on the original text-model setup.
record.method_sensitivity: Tokenization changes fitted loss coefficients and downstream scaling: unigram-compressed tokens have different fitted α and β values and worse downstream scaling than raw HuBERT tokens. The authors also state that downstream curves saturate, which limits extrapolation.

fits_no_version.finding: Pre-training on synthetic sTinyStories improves Topic and Story Cloze across model scales.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Data composition, not only scale, shifts downstream semantic performance of speech LMs.

fits_no_version.finding: Linguistic performance of speech LMs scales up to about 10^3 times more slowly with compute than text LMs (γq ratios 3.14, 1.56, 2.7).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Downstream scaling efficiency differs strongly across modalities.

record.peer_reviewed: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing, 2024
record.problems: The paper notes that downstream scaling fits ignore metric saturation, that the Pythia models used may be overtrained, and that the minimal-loss-per-FLOP envelope may have slight negative curvature at larger scale. Unigram-token experiments are limited to models up to 309M parameters and have no multi-epoch runs. No uncertainty estimates or out-of-sample small-to-large prediction test are reported.
record.rows_left_out: No numerical per-model curve values are stated in the text for Figures 1–5, so aggregate textual conclusions and the tabulated fit coefficients are recorded instead. Table 3 benchmarking results, cited results from prior work, and the synthetic Tiny Stories training comparison are omitted because they do not directly measure the listed scaling or predictability versions.

untested.parts: No test of small-run fits predicting much larger runs. The Limitations section says extrapolations should be considered optimistic.
No shape or architecture variation at fixed parameter count.
Only speech is tested. Image, video, fine-tuning and transfer are not.
Text-model loss scaling is not measured; the text fit in Table 5 is cited from Muennighoff et al. Speech models only go up to 823M parameters.

missing.what: Upstream loss of unigram-token SLMs scales similarly with compute; the caption says it scales better than raw tokens.
RN* > RD* in speech, unlike text: repeated tokens decay faster than excess parameters.

record.verdict_notes: The reader labelled V5 limits_scope and V7 limits_scope using r17/r18. Those rows are downstream measures and do not bear on V5 (loss power-law form) or V7 (loss-fit exponents and split), so those labels were dropped and replaced. The Table 5 text row (Muennighoff) is cited, not this study's result. The negative curvature in the Limitations section is a cited caveat, not a finding. No uncertainty is reported on the fits.

versions.untested_parts: Tests held-out loss scaling in speech language models; does not test all language-model modalities or establish the claim across the full range of text-model setups.
No explicit test of whether fits on small runs predict runs orders of magnitude larger.
Tests fitted compute-optimal allocations for speech models, including raw and unigram tokens; does not test the competing Kaplan and Hoffmann trends across text-model setups.
No controlled test of depth, width, or architecture variation at fixed parameter count.
Tests speech models and two speech-tokenization setups, not image/video modalities, fine-tuning, transfer, or other training regimes.
Tests BLIMP, Topic Cloze, and Story Cloze scaling and their association with test loss; does not test broader downstream tasks.

Shows differences between raw and unigram tokenization fits and downstream curves; does not systematically vary parameter counting, fitting method, schedule, or data to establish the full range of causes of published-law disagreement.

relationships.reason: The single-epoch minimal-loss-per-FLOP envelope follows a power law (r1), and the parametric fit gives α=0.25, β=0.24 (r2).
relationships.display_finding: The single-epoch compute-efficient loss envelope followed a power law, with parametric exponents α = 0.25 and β = 0.24.

relationships.reason: Metrics are strongly linearly correlated with test loss (r8–r10) and follow power laws in compute (r11–r16). Speech exponents are smaller.

relationships.reason: Downstream scaling is worse than with raw tokens (r17), and Story Cloze does not improve with compute (r18), even though upstream loss scales fine.
relationships.display_finding: Downstream performance scaled worse than with raw tokens, and Story Cloze did not improve with compute despite upstream loss scaling.

source_check.label: limits_scope
source_check.reason: The condition group has worse downstream scaling despite upstream scaling, including explicitly absent improvement on Story Cloze (r17, r18).

relationships.condition: Raw versus unigram tokenization of the same speech data
relationships.reason: The fitted exponents shift with tokenization: α 0.25→0.15 and β 0.24→0.16 (r2, r3).
relationships.display_finding: Switching from raw to unigram tokenization changes α from 0.25 to 0.15 and β from 0.24 to 0.16 on the same speech data.

source_check.label: supports
source_check.condition: Raw versus unigram tokenization of the same speech data
source_check.reason: Table 5 shows that changing tokenization changes α/β from 0.25/0.24 to 0.15/0.16 (r2, r3).

relationships.reason: Despite the different exponents, the optimal N/D split stays about equal in both fits (r4–r7). This setup choice did not move the split.
relationships.display_finding: Both tokenizations retained an approximately equal compute-optimal model/data split despite differing fitted loss exponents.

source_check.label: limits_scope
source_check.reason: The tokenization comparison changes loss exponents while retaining approximately equal parameter/data growth exponents, qualifying any claim that both must change together (r2–r7).
